# hypothesis: An Any-typed value flows into a precise int parameter with no error, while an object-typed argument is rejected by checkers, yet CPython runs the call and returns the same result.
from typing import Any, assert_type, reveal_type


def double(n: int) -> int:
    return n * 2


def relay(v: Any) -> Any:
    return v


def use_object(o: object) -> int:
    return double(o)  # expect-error: object is not int


raw: Any = 21
r = relay(raw)
reveal_type(r)
assert_type(double(r), int)
assert double(r) == 42

xs: list[Any] = [1, 'a', None]
first = xs[0]
reveal_type(first)
assert_type(first, Any)
assert use_object(5) == 10
hypothesis: An Any-typed value flows into a precise int parameter without a checker error, while an object-typed argument is rejected statically, yet CPython runs both calls and returns the same results.
